The Thomas Cook India Group 
(‘The Group
’) is pleased to present 
its Integrated Annual Report for 
FY 2024-25. The Report includes 
a comprehensive and transparent 
disclosure of the ﬁnancial and 
non-ﬁnancial parameters, with an 
endeavour to create long-term value 
for all its stakeholders. It adheres to the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015.
This <IR> encompasses Thomas 
Cook India Group’s overall ﬁnancial 
and non-ﬁnancial performance for FY 
2024-25. It covers ﬁnancial highlights, 
strategic priorities, macroeconomic 
environment, risks and opportunities, 
governance structures, challenges, and 
achievements of its growth journey. Reporting Period
The <IR>, published annually, contains 
essential information concerning the 
progress and advancements of the 
organisation during the period from 
April 01, 2024, to March 31, 2025. It 
presents material details about the 
Company’s developments and activities 
within this timeframe.
Reporting Boundary and 
Scope
This Report includes comprehensive 
information about the Thomas Cook 
India Group, including its main entity, 
Thomas Cook (India) Limited (also 
referred to as ‘Thomas Cook India,’ 
‘Thomas Cook,’ ‘TCIL,’ ‘The Company,’ 
or ‘We’),, as well as its subsidiary 
companies and signiﬁcant investments 
both in India and globally. It oﬀers a 
thorough evaluation of the Group’s 
business model, strategic priorities, 
and associated risks, with the aim of 
presenting a holistic view of its long-
term sustainability.
Reporting Principle
This Report adheres to the <IR> 
framework established by the 
International Integrated Reporting 
Council (IIRC). Its ﬁnancial and statutory 
information complies with the necessary 
regulations, including the Companies 
Act, 2013, Indian Accounting Standards, 
Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and 
the Secretarial Standards. For detailed 
independent auditor’s reports on 
both the standalone and consolidated 
ﬁnancial statements, please refer to 
pages 206 and 299, respectively.Non-Financial R
eporting
In addition to ﬁnancial reporting, 
this report provides a wide range of 
information, including non-ﬁnancial 
performance indicators, opportunities, 
risks, and strategies for risk mitigation, 
and extends beyond ﬁnancial 
reporting. It also highlights outcomes 
that are attributable to or connected 
with our key stakeholders, and 
signiﬁcantly impact our value creation. 
It also provides a comprehensive view 
of the Company’s performance and 
the various factors that contribute to 
its overall success, extending beyond 
traditional ﬁnancial aspects.
Board and Management 
Assurance
The Board of Directors and our 
Management are fully committed to 
ensuring the accuracy and reliability 
of this <IR>. They are conﬁdent that 
it provides a fair and comprehensive 
representation of the overall 
performance of the Company and 
its impact. All ﬁnancial statements 
included in this Report pertain to the 
period ending on March 31, 2025, and 
cover the entirety of the ﬁscal year up

For over a century
, Thomas 
Cook has earned this trust 
by transforming journeys into

by the Fairfax Group (63.83%

leading integrated travel and

countries across 5 continents, 
covering every aspect of the 
travel lifecycle, from planning 
to execution, from currency to

From the 
Chairman
’s Desk
Dear Directors, Shareholders, P
artners, and Colleagues,
It is with a sense of pride that I present to you the Annual Report of Thomas Cook (India) Limited for 
FY 2024-25. The last twelve months have seen the travel industry go through one of the most 
unpredictable environments in recent memory. Global travel and tourism, while rebounding in many ways 
post pandemic, was disrupted by mounting global geopolitical tensions, economic headwinds, ﬂuctuating 
currencies, and supply chain fragilities. The ripple eﬀects of conﬂicts, energy volatility and policy shifts 
across borders have been felt even in the farthest corners of the travel ecosystem. Despite these 
headwinds, the Company remained resilient, agile and committed to building trust: investing in people, 
technology and a deep understanding of customers' evolving needs. Madhavan MenonYour Company’s record 
financial performance was 
endorsed by CRISIL on June 
24, 2025, with an upgradation 
of the Group’s ratings to 
CRISIL AA/Stable/CRISIL A1+, 
the highest rating achieved by 
your Company in its historyIntegrated 
Annual Report 2024-25
14
Building T
rust, with 
Strong Financial 
Performance  
Your Company achieved record proﬁts 
during FY 2024-25 with the highest 
ever consolidated PBT of /uni20B9/uni00A03,821 mn 
with a growth of 11%. Total income 
grew by 11% y-o-y to /uni20B9 82,845 mn.
Travel Services EBIT grew by 29% 
in FY 2024-25, aided by a strong 
turnaround of global DMS companies, 
led by Asian Trails (Asia-Paciﬁc), Allied 
T-Pro (Americas), Desert Adventures 
(GCC Region), and Private Safaris 
(South Africa), which grew by 23% 
year-on-year. Forex EBIT grew by 
21%, led by the overseas education 
and retail segments. Sterling Holiday 
Resorts recorded a 10% growth in 
sales, registering 20 consecutive 
proﬁtable quarters and adding 11 new 
resorts during the ﬁscal year, bringing 
its portfolio to 61 resorts.
Your Company’s record ﬁnancial 
performance was endorsed by 
CRISIL on June 24, 2025, with an 
upgradation of the Group’s ratings 
to CRISIL AA/Stable/CRISIL A1+, 
the highest rating achieved by 
your Company in its history and 
the highest credit rating for any 
travel and tourism company in 
the country. The upgraded ratings 
reﬂect your Company’s strong 
business risk proﬁle and leadership 
position in travel and foreign 
exchange segments. Additionally, 
acknowledgment of structural 
reduction in cost, resulting in better 
operating margin and ROCE; also 
improved the ﬁnancial risk proﬁle 
following sustained healthy operating 
performance, as reﬂected in your 
Company’s adequate capital structure 
and strong liquid surpluses. The 
upgraded rating of the parent, Fairfax 
Financial Holdings Limited and 
continued support has added to the 
Group’s stability.In February 2025, your Company 
entered an agreement with Sterling 
Holiday Resorts to integrate its Nature 
Trails brand, operational retreats and 
teams into your Company’s domestic 
operations. Nature Trails operates on an 
asset-light model with resorts at scenic 
locations in Maharashtra, amidst natural 
surroundings. Nature Trails oﬀers activity 
led holidays and experiences across 
multiple market segments including:
Adventure Holidays
With experiences such as trekking, 
kayaking, rafting, and zip lining
Educational T
rips
include survival skills, self-defence, 
nature-appreciation, among others, 
towards resilience/adaptability for 
students and corporates
Corporate Getaways
For team building activities, wellness and 
leadership development programmes, 
among others.
This integration reinforces our 
commitment to India’s domestic tourism 
sector. 
More recently, in May 2025, we 
established our presence in the 
European Union (EU) by setting up an 
oﬃce in Nicosia (Cyprus). The newly 
formed entity, Travel Circle International 
(Cyprus) Limited, will focus on the 
business travel requirements of both 
multinational companies and India-based 
corporate clients, with a presence in 
Europe.
Building Trust, with 
Innovation and 
Technology
Innovation and technology continue 
to be cornerstones of your Company’s 
customer-ﬁrst strategy. 
AI-Powered Initiatives
Your Company has invested in AI-
driven business solutions and customer 
experience to serve a new generation of digital ﬁrst customers with its JV 
partner, Atirath Technologies Private 
Limited. These steps are not only 
about improving eﬃciency but also 
about building a more personalised 
and seamless customer journey. 
Your Company has launched GenAI 
chatbots Tacy (for Thomas Cook) and 
Ezy (for SOTC) that seamlessly allow 
website visitors to have a complete 
handheld, eﬃcient interaction without 
needing to speak to anyone. These will 
soon be upgraded with a multilingual 
voice capability for those who prefer 
voice interactions over text. A valuable 
quality check AI tool has been 
deployed at your Company’s contact 
centres - that listens in to calls and 
provides valuable recommendations 
that are then used for training and up-
skilling agents. 
Your Company’s pioneering initiatives 
include the launch of Dhruv - India’s 
ﬁrst multi-modal, multi-lingual, agentic 
voice and Email GenAI advisor - that 
harnesses AI and Large Language 
Models (LLMs) to address the rapidly 
growing and evolving needs of India’s 
business travel sector. 
With a focus on empowering both 
sales teams and end customers, your 
Company’s AI-powered dynamic 
itinerary builder has been equipped 
with pricing and booking capabilities 
for end-to-end holiday transactions. 
Empowering Customers with 
Self-Service Tools
Corporate Travel’s digital forward 
strategy saw the launch of Travel 
One, an online self-booking tool, 
built in-house. Strong adoption has 
resulted in noteworthy 56% touchless 
transactions this ﬁscal. The Customer 
self-service app gives leisure travellers 
control over their post-booking 
journey: from visa information and 
tracking to downloading of vouchers, 
itineraries, and invoices for a seamless 
experience.

Building T
rust by 
Investing in People 
Your Company’s people-ﬁrst 
philosophy focusses on building 
future leaders via a Management 
Development Programme (MDP), 
an immersive six-day residential 
experience tailored for emerging 
and mid-level managers, blending 
experiential learning, business 
simulations, cross-functional case 
studies, inspiring keynote sessions and 
collaborative team-based challenges. 
Your Company’s people also beneﬁt 
from 24x7 access to self-paced 
online learning resources, supporting 
development in today’s fast-paced 
environment. Emphasis on continuous 
learning reinforces this vision. We 
deliver structured training interventions 
that enhance both functional expertise 
and essential soft skills, particularly for 
TCIL’s frontline teams who serve as the 
face of our brand. 
Successful implementation of a 
succession planning framework 
enables us to proactively identify and 
prepare high-potential employees for 
critical roles. This ensures leadership 
continuity, strengthens organisational 
agility, and promotes measurable 
success through internal promotions. 
It is a testament to the strength and 
depth of our internal talent pipeline.
Building Trust via CSR, 
ESG Initiatives and 
Partnering with the 
Government
CSR Initiatives
Your Company has a focused 
Corporate Social Responsibility 
programme, delivered via the Fairfax 
India Charitable Foundation (FICF) - a 
registered public charitable trust, 
certiﬁed under Sections 80G and 
12AA of the Income Tax Act and under 
CSR-1. FICF’s core mission is to expand 
access to quality and aﬀordable 
dialysis care, particularly in rural and 
underserved regions across India 
where Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) 
is increasing at an alarming pace, 
with approximately 1.3 mn patients 
requiring dialysis 2-3 times a week to 
survive. 
To address this challenge, FICF has 
actively collaborated with various 
state governments and charitable 
hospitals across the nation, and to 
date, facilitated the installation of 
over 1,425 dialysis machines across 
355 centres in 270 districts spanning 
28 states and /U.smcpnion territories. 
Collectively, these centres have 
delivered over 2.9 mn free dialysis 
sessions, serving thousands of 
patients and signiﬁcantly easing 
the burden on public healthcare 
infrastructure by serving over 31% of 
India’s rural population with dialysis 
service closer to their homes. By 
ensuring proximity and free dialysis 
to BPL patients, these eﬀorts have 
helped deserving patients save 
approximately /uni20B9 5.8 bn so far and 
created 3,550 jobs for the local 
community. FICF is proud to support 
the Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis 
Programme (PMNDP) with 10% of all 
the dialysis machines under PMNDP, 
installed via FICF’s Dialysis mission.
FICF’s goal is to take dialysis access 
to over 45% of India’s rural population 
with 2,000 dialysis machines across 
450 dialysis centres across 350 
districts in 30 states and union 
territories.
ESG Initiatives
Across your Company, we are driving 
planet-friendly initiatives such as 
minimising paper consumption, using 
sustainable materials, improving 
energy eﬃciency, implementing 
waste management initiatives, and 
promoting water conservation.Notable ESG Initiatives by Your 
Company’s Subsidiaries
Travel Corporation (India) Limited is a 
signatory to the Glasgow Declaration, 
committed to cut tourism emissions 
by half over the next decade and 
reach Net Zero emissions before 
2050. TCI has also initiated aﬃliation 
with Travelife, a leading international 
training, management and certiﬁcation 
programme for sustainable travel 
organisations. 
Through SANKALP, Sterling continues 
to champion responsible tourism, 
balancing growth with purpose, 
performance with conscience, and 
every guest stay with positive impact. 
We have made meaningful progress in 
enhancing our sustainability practices, 
including upgrades to energy-eﬃcient 
systems, adoption of green cooling 
technologies, and water conservation 
initiatives across our resorts. These 
eﬀorts, being implemented in a phased 
manner, reﬂect our deep commitment 
to embedding ESG at the core of our 
operations while delivering long-term 
value to all stakeholders.

Building T
rust and 
Navigating Uncertainty 
with Conﬁdence
In this increasingly Volatile, Uncertain, 
Complex, and Ambiguous (VUCA) 
world, TCIL’s strategic focus will be on 
providing what customers and partners 
value most: Trust. The learnings from 
these disruptions helped us curate 
a comprehensive programme called 
TravSure to reassure customers that 
they would be taken care of, in an 
increasingly unpredictable travel 
environment. TravSure is a truly unique 
service oﬀering, giving customers 
the conﬁdence to travel in uncertain 
times. It oﬀers free cancellation and 
rescheduling in case of unforeseen 
emergencies, additional trip protection 
in non-standard emergencies 
such as wars or war-like situations, 
closure of air space and temporary 
accommodation or food. TravSure 
services also include a dedicated 24x7 
emergency customer support service 
to assist customers.Looking Ahead
The global environment is likely to 
become more unpredictable. However, 
we will remain unwavering in our 
commitment to building trust and 
resilience among our customers. As 
India continues its journey as one 
of the world’s fastest growing and 
dynamic travel markets, with the 
growing global opportunities for TCIL’s 
services, we believe we should not 
merely scale fast, but do so with trust 
and integrity.

As you are aware, I have stepped 
down as the Executive Chairman of the

memories of which I will cherish for

that your Company stands on a ﬁrm

to scale new heights. It is precisely for

had come for me to retire and hand

experience, wherewithal, and skills to 
scale new heights.

objective. Your Company has been

productivity, among others, to remain

been facilitated by good governance,

Launch of Borderless Travel Prepaid Forex Card
TCIL has strategically launched the Borderless Travel Prepaid Forex Card in alignment 
with India’s booming outbound travel market. Developed in partnership with global 
payment leaders Mastercard and Visa, the card represents a signiﬁcant innovation 
in travel convenience and sustainability. Notably, it is India’s ﬁrst eco-friendly holiday 
travel card made from recycled plastic, underlining the company’s commitment to 
responsible travel solutions. This launch further strengthens Thomas Cook's leadership 
as ‘India ka Forex Specialist,’ reinforcing its expertise and pioneering status in the 
foreign exchange space.
Key Features
 Multi-Currency:  Supports 12 currencies; seamless wallet shift
 Security:  Chip and PIN enabled, insurance cover up to /uni20B9 7 .5 lakhs, emergency  
cash facility
 Travel Privileges: Free lounge access, airport porter and meet-greet services (India)
 Global Access: Accepted at 70 mn+ merchants and 3 mn+ A TMs  
(Mastercard and Visa)
 Extras:  24x7 support, eco-friendly (recycled plastic)
Strategic Initiatives
 Our sharp focus on retail-led 
growth, particularly in education 
and holiday segments, has paid 
dividends.
 Digital transformation through 
WhatsApp Bookings and Callings, 
V-KYC, and FXNOW is enabling 
technical promotion, oﬀering deals 
and vouchers, and supporting faster 
scalability with reduced friction.
 With the launch of the BPC T ravel 
Card in the holiday segment, in the 
forex prepaid card segment, we 
have separate products meeting 
the needs of each of travel 
segments – Holiday, Education and 
Corporate Travel
 We operate as India’s largest 
Omnichannel FX Network, 
comprising over 4,000 touchpoints 
across the country. This expansive 
network is powered by an asset-
light strategy that leverages 
partner agents instead of fully 
owned branches, enabling wide 
market coverage with lower capital 
investment. We are future-ready for regulatory 
tailwinds such as Forex

Network Expansion
TCIL and our group company SOTC Travel introduced TravSure, a pioneering 
travel safety programme designed to boost traveller conﬁdence amidst ongoing 
global uncertainties. This industry-ﬁrst initiative oﬀers comprehensive emergency 
protection for international group tour travellers, covering disruptions such as ﬂight 
suspensions, war-like situations, political unrest, riots, and airspace closures – 
events typically excluded from standard travel insurance. TravSure also includes free 
rescheduling and refunds for unutilised services, additional ﬁnancial coverage of up 
to USD 1,500 per person for unexpected rescheduling or hotel stays, and 24/7 real-
time customer support through dedicated representatives. With a focus on today’s 
evolving traveller mindset, TravSure aims to deliver peace of mind and empower 
travellers to explore the world securely and conﬁdently.

STUDYIntegrated 
Annual Report 2024-25
44
STUDYBuilding Lasting Trust 
Through Exceptional 
Experiences
In 2025, what began as a landmark incentive trip to London for 625 
delegates quickly turned into a test of resilience. Sudden airspace 
closures and airline disruptions across the Middle East caused mass 
ﬂight cancellations, leaving 85 delegates stranded in London for 
three extra nights and 55 more stuck in transit at Doha Airport. As 
uncertainty mounted and emotions ran high, our teams sprang into 
action-securing emergency accommodations, managing ground 
logistics, calming anxious travellers, and even personally caring for a 
delegate in isolation. Behind the scenes, our airline operations team 
worked tirelessly to rebook passengers through alternative hubs, while 
strong leadership enabled swift decision-making and uniﬁed team 
eﬀorts. Despite the chaos, every delegate returned home safely. The 
client’s heartfelt appreciation turned a potential crisis into a story of 
grit, compassion, and seamless execution.

End-to-end Non-Air and Car-Related Travel ServicesDhruv AI Launch
In partnership with LTIMindtree, Voicing.AI, and Fairfax Digital Services, we launched Dhruv AI, India’s first agentic AI travel advisor, designed to transform the corporate travel experience through intelligent, real-time support. Built on custom-trained Large Language Models, Dhruv is multilingual (supporting over 20 Indian and global languages) and multimodal, operating seamlessly across chat, voice, email, and mobile interfaces. It provides smart insights on travel policy gaps, supplier performance, and cost optimisation, while enabling conversational support with human-like empathy. This AI innovation not only enhances customer experience but also drives operational efficiency and scalability across our travel ecosystem.
Integrated Travel and 
Expense Management
In our endeavour to increase digital 
adoption and provide customers with end-to-end travel and expense solutions, we forged a strategic alliance with Zaggle, a leading SaaS FinTech company specialising in spend management and embedded finance. Zaggle’s platform offers a comprehensive suite of tools including expense automation, corporate cards, employee reimbursements, petty cash control, and procurement workflows. Their solutions are built to seamlessly integrate with ERP and HRMS systems, allowing businesses to manage the entire expense lifecycle, from booking to reconciliation, on a single, unified platform. This partnership strengthens our offering by combining travel services with real-time expense visibility, enhanced policy compliance, and operational efficiency, enabling clients to gain tighter control over travel-related spends while improving the employee experience.
Sustainability Integration
As business travel scales back up, the focus on sustainability is sharper than ever. Companies are expected to track, reduce, and offset their travel-related emissions. In line with this increased focus on sustainability, we continued our partnership with Green Carpet, a global platform to monitor, manage and report travel emissions. Developed in collaboration with LTIMindtree, we offer clients curated sustainable travel solutions, ranging from eco-certified hotels and low-emission transport options to carbon tracking tools and verified offset programmes. This initiative supports corporate ESG objectives while ensuring a seamless and responsible travel experience.
Client Growth
Across TCIL and SOTC, we continued our rigorous focus on new client acquisitions, registering some marquee client acquisitions in retail, FMCG, IT & ITS, and pharmaceutical sectors. The total travel spends of these clients amounted to an aggregate over ₹ 300 crores. There was a renewed focus, specifically in the areas of prospecting and lead generation, where we forged lead-sharing partnerships with Corporate Travel Card platforms like SBI CTA. In addition to the same, we have partnered with the Global Business Travel Association (GBTA), wherein, Prasad Shriyan, our VP of Business Transformation is now on the India Advisory Board of GBTA, which gives us networking opportunities and access to travel buyers and suppliers, not only across India, but also in Asia-Pacific and around the globe. We also continued our efforts on acquiring new business through our strategic partnerships with CTM, a leading global travel management company known for its technology-driven, high-touch service model and OneGlobal, which is one of the leading global consortiums of  best-in-class corporate travel providers. These partnerships give us an opportunity to acquire high-value and high-margin global clients which would eventually lead to better revenue and EBIT realisations overall.
Global Expansion
In line with our strategy to expand our client base beyond India and develop capability to expand our business travel offerings to our existing customers in the European market, we inaugurated Travel Circle International (Cyprus) Ltd (TCI Euro), our first European Union office based in Nicosia, Cyprus. TCI Euro offers clients access to local EU pricing, regional inventory, and seamless travel solutions, enhancing efficiency and cost-effectiveness for cross-border travel within the region.

At TCIL, we deeply understand the intrinsic

FICF’
s ﬂagship mission is to make critical

free or aﬀordable dialysis services to

regions across India where such life-
saving treatments are either unavailable 
or unaﬀordable, FICF is actively working

Project DialysisSocial Impact Delivered (as of March 2025)
Our Mission
To build a high-impact, sustainable, 
and collaborative ecosystem that 
delivers free or aﬀordable, high-
quality dialysis services to renal 
patients in regions of India with 
limited or no dialysis infrastructure.
Background
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) aﬀects 
nearly one in seven adults in India. Over 
1.3 mn individuals require dialysis two to 
three times a week to survive. However, 
only about 15% of these patients 
currently have access to this critical 
treatment-largely due to the prohibitive 
cost and lack of nearby facilities.
India faces a severe shortage of dialysis 
infrastructure. While an estimated 
200,000 machines are needed 
nationwide, only around 35,000 are 
operational, of which more than 80% 
serve urban and aﬄuent populations, 
leaving rural and low-income 
communities vastly underserved. 
Project Implementation
Project 
Dialysis is implemented through 
a robust public-private partnership 
(PPP) model, aligned with the Pradhan 
Mantri National Dialysis Programme 
and supported by state governments. 
This collaborative model combines 
government infrastructure, private 
healthcare expertise, and corporate 
funding to deliver meaningful and 
scalable outcomes.
A comprehensive nationwide 
assessment, covering the prevalence 
of kidney failure, availability of existing 
dialysis facilities, and estimated patient 
needs, enables us to identify high-
priority areas. Through extensive 
stakeholder consultations, we select 
project sites strategically to maximise 
reach and impact.
Each project is executed with 
precision-clearly deﬁning roles and 
responsibilities of all stakeholders to 
prevent overlap, ensure accountability, 
and guarantee long-term sustainability. 
Partner selection is driven by capability and commitment, and a rigorous 
implementation roadmap ensures timely 
deployment and continuous monitoring.
Driving Quality Through 
Automation and Technology
To deliver consistently high standards of 
care, we equip centres with state-of-the-
art dialysis machines featuring advanced 
automation and integrated data systems to 
support audits and track outcomes. Each 
centre is staﬀed with skilled healthcare 
professionals and adheres to protocols 
comparable to top-tier private facilities.
Patients beneﬁt from a seamless 
experience, supported by an informative 
and easy-to-navigate website oﬀering 
details on centre locations, directions, 
and contact information. Vivid imagery 
showcases the modern, patient-centric 
environment within each facility-oﬀering 
reassurance and dignity to those who rely 
on our services.

Strengthening Waste 
Management Practices
TCIL has implemented a multi-pronged 
waste management strategy across its 
facilities:
 We operate STPs and organic 
waste converters to process waste 
eﬃciently and generate compost.
 Our cleaning protocols rely on 
eco-friendly products that reduce 
chemical discharge into the 
environment.
 Kitchen waste is converted into 
nutrient-rich organic compost, 
contributing to a circular economy.
 Paper waste is recycled into 
biodegradable stationery, including 
pens, pencils, and writing pads.
 As part of our plastic reduction 
goals, we have discontinued the 
use of pre-packaged plastic water 
bottles in our oﬃces.Conserving  
Water Resources
Water conservation is integral to 
our environmental initiatives. At our 
Mumbai headquarters, several steps 
have been taken:
 STPs help treat and reuse 
wastewater, reducing the discharge 
and improving water-use eﬃciency.
 Rainwater harvesting systems 
collect and store rainwater, 
reducing dependence on municipal 
sources.
 Recycled water is used for WC 
ﬂushing.
 Sprinkler nozzles have been 
installed in hand-wash areas to 
reduce water ﬂow, and bio-based 
cleaning products are used to 
minimise chemical contamination.Optimising  
Energy Consumption
We have adopted a range of energy 
eﬃciency measures to reduce 
consumption and carbon emissions:
 LED lighting, which uses over 90% 
less energy than traditional lighting, 
has been widely adopted across 
our premises.
 Our oﬃces are designed to 
maximise the use of natural 
daylight, reducing the need for 
artiﬁcial lighting.
 Solar energy systems, including 
water heaters and heat pumps, 
reduce reliance on conventional 
power sources.
 We are piloting the use of IoT- 
and AI-based devices on split 
and cassette air conditioners to 
optimise energy usage. Initial 
installations in select branches 
have shown promising results and 
will be scaled to other locations for 
further energy savings and carbon 
footprint reduction.02
Reducing Paper Usage and Conserving Natural Resources
As part of our long-standing commitment to environmental stewardship, TCIL is actively reducing paper consumption and 
promoting aﬀorestation:
 We conduct tree-planting drives at our holiday resorts as part of our green initiatives.
 Digital transformation through e-invoicing and electronic report dissemination signiﬁcantly reduces our dependency on paper.
 Sustainable materials have been used in oﬃce refurbishments wherever possible, including eco-friendly Bharat Tiles, low-VOC 
paints, durable cables, toughened glass, and Relwood composite panels.

ESG in Action through SANKALP
At Sterling Holiday 
Resorts, sustainability is not an afterthought; it is woven into the fabric of our operations. Rooted in the Sanskrit word SANKALP, meaning ‘pledge,’ the programme embodies our unwavering commitment to responsible tourism, environmental stewardship, and community well-being.
Through SANKALP, we 
have institutionalised our ESG principles, driving meaningful outcomes across environmental, social, and governance dimensions.SANKALP places equal emphasis on social impact, with initiatives designed to uplift communities and enhance employee well-being.
In partnership with the Fairfax India Charitable Foundation (FICF) under 
Project Dialysis, Sterling installed 16 dialysis machines in underserved districts and committed ₹ 15 mn in FY 2024-25 to procuring 22 additional machines. These efforts are expected to enable over 18,000 subsidised dialysis sessions annually, potentially saving patients approximately ₹ 36.4 mn while reducing pressure on the public healthcare system.
Employee wellness remained a key priority, with the Company launching 
comprehensive health screenings for all employees aged 50 and aligned, aligned with Fairfax’s broader ESG directive on workplace health.
On the governance front, Sterling continues to operate with integrity and 
accountability. The Company adheres to the Fairfax Code of Conduct and aligns with TCIL’s governance framework, ensuring robust internal controls, transparent practices, and a commitment to community-focused leadership.

Electrical Efficiency 
Enhancements
 CFL and CCFL fixtures

 Motion sensors and timers help extend lamp life and further conserve energy.
 It has begun upgrading transformers at larger resorts to high-efficiency Type 2 models that minimise transfer losses and offer improved voltage regulation and system protection.
Solar Energy Pilot Projects
 Pilot solar energy projects have been initiated at three resorts to generate or pre-heat water.
 These efforts reflect SHRL’ s strategic shift towards 
renewable energy and carbon footprint reduction.Smart  
Cooling Systems
 Traditional split AC units 
are being replaced with inverter-based systems for greater energy efficiency
.
 In colder regions, Variable R
efrigerant 
Flow (VRF) systems are being deployed for dual-purpose heating and cooling, replacing less efficient heaters and reducing energy load.
 Old split units are being replaced with highly efficient variable frequency flow heat pump systems using green refrigerants for space conditioning.
Elimination of Bottled Water with Centralised Water 
Stations
 A filtration-cum-bottling plant has been piloted to provide 
safe, refillable water stations at resorts, replacing single-use plastic bottles and curbing plastic waste
.Water Efficiency and 
Plumbing Upgrades
 Outdated monobloc 
pumps have been substituted with high-efficiency, multi-stage pumps equipped with V
ariable Frequency 
Drives (VFDs).
 Water-saving fixtures such as aerators, flow restrictors, and dual flush systems have been introduced.
 Rainwater harvesting infrastructure is being installed at larger resorts to supplement freshwater sources or recharge aquifers.
 Replacing the conventional faucets with automatic faucets for optimal water use
.
Supporting Green Mobility
 In collaboration with regional partners, SHRL is rolling out fast-charging DC stations for electric vehicles at all resorts, encouraging EV usage and reducing transport-related emissions.Adoption of Heat Pump 
Technology
 SHRL is phasing out 
conventional geysers and HSD-powered water heaters, replacing them with energy-efficient heat pump systems.
 In several locations, solar panels are used for preheating water, further reducing electricity and fossil fuel use
.

six resorts have been completed, with work in progress at three additional locations.

champion green strategies across oﬃces. In line with 
its sustainability goals, Private Safaris Southern Africa 
is actively working towards Travelife certiﬁcation within 
the next three years—a globally recognised standard 
for sustainable tourism.
Private Safaris East Africa sustainability framework 
is built on ﬁve key pillars that holistically address 
environmental, social, and governance (ESG) 
priorities. From an environmental standpoint, the 
company champions waste reduction by eliminating 
single-use plastics, has gone paperless through 
digital transformation, and promotes eco-certiﬁed 
accommodations alongside conservation partnerships 
with the Kenya Wildlife Society and Kenya Eco 
Tourism Society. Socially, it actively supports local 
artisans and guides, invests in employee welfare 
through fair wages and development, and promotes 
cultural awareness and high safety standards. On 
the governance front, it upholds ethical business 
practices, fair labour, regulatory compliance, and 
fosters sustainable partnerships. Its accessibility 
initiatives include inclusive tourism for travellers with 
mobility needs and career development opportunities 
through collaborations with institutions like Utalii College. Looking ahead, Private Safaris East Africa 
remains committed to continuous improvement, deeper 
community engagement, and scaling conservation 
eﬀorts, laying the foundation for a more equitable and 
sustainable travel ecosystem.
As part of its ongoing commitment to sustainability and 
fostering an environmentally responsible workplace, 
Desert Adventures has introduced several green 
initiatives in its oﬃce. To reduce single-use plastic waste, 
it has stopped providing bottled water, installed water 
puriﬁers in the pantries, and provided all team members 
with reusable bottles. Glass water jars and paper cups 
are available in the reception, meeting rooms, and 
common pantry to ensure easy access to clean drinking 
water for staﬀ and visitors. It is also reducing paper 
usage by minimising printing and transitioning to digital 
documentation, using electronic signature for most 
agreements and contracts.
Asian Trails continued to embed sustainability 
across all areas of its business, guided by its ESTEEM 
principles. The company emphasized local community 
engagement, eco-friendly travel choices, and ethical 
tourism experiences, including the rollout of ten 
Explore Guides and updated Responsible Animal 
Experiences manuals. All staﬀ received monthly training 
on practical sustainability topics. A key milestone 
was reaching Travelife Partner status in Indonesia, 
Myanmar, and Vietnam, while renewal of this designation 
was underway in Cambodia, China, Laos, Malaysia, 
and Thailand. The Travelife Partner award conﬁrms 
compliance with over 100 sustainability criteria, and 
Asian Trails is working toward eventual Travelife 
Certiﬁed status. Complementary initiatives included 
carbon tracking via the Carmacal platform, support for 
reﬁllable water bottle use, and partnerships like Hotel 
Resilient to promote responsible accommodation. CSR 
engagement was widespread across oﬃces, reinforcing 
sustainability as a shared responsibility within the 
organisation.Integrated

Opportunity and RiskRisk Management
At Thomas Cook, we place strong emphasis on a robust risk management framework to eﬀectively navigate the complexities 
of our multinational operations. Our integrated approach encompasses ongoing risk identiﬁcation, assessment, mitigation, 
monitoring, and reporting. By aligning risk management with our strategic goals, we adopt a holistic stance that not only 
addresses potential threats but also capitalises on emerging opportunities. This proactive and structured approach enables us to 
drive sustainable growth, build organisational resilience, and uphold the long-term trust of our stakeholders.

TO THE MEMBERS,
Your Directors have pleasure in presenting the Forty-Eighth 
Annual Report, together with Audited Financial Statements for 
the financial year ended on March 31, 2025.
O
VERVIEW
The World Travel and Tourism’s contribution to global GDP 
totaled $ 11.7 Tn. As a share, Travel & Tourism represented this 
year, 10.3% of global GDP , while jobs supported by the sector 
are expected to rise by 14 Mn, reaching 371 Mn worldwide. By 
2034, travel and tourism is projected to contribute $ 16 Tn to 
global GDP (more than 11% globally), supporting businesses, 
destinations and local communities while facilitating 
approximately 30 billion tourist visits worldwide (domestic and 
international). 
Travel & Tourism’s economic influence extends beyond airlines 
and hospitality companies into local economies through 
extensive supply chains supporting agricultural producers, food 
service providers, retail establishments, financial institutions 
and countless small businesses. Indeed, more than two-thirds 
of the sector’s economic contribution flows through indirect or 
induced channels, including supply chain effects, government 
spending and capital investment.
The Indian travel and tourism industry is a significant sector 
within the Indian economy, projected to generate revenue 
exceeding $ 59 Bn by CY 2028, which is over ` 5,12,356 crores. 
Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs) are expected to reach 30.5 Mn 
by CY 2028, a substantial increase from 9.52 Mn in CY 2023, 
which saw a 47.9% growth compared to the previous year. The 
travel market in India is expected to reach $ 125 Bn by FY 2026-
27, up from an estimated $ 75 Bn in FY 2019-20. 
According to World Travel & Tourism Council, the industry is 
expected to grow at an annual rate of 7.1% in the coming decade, 
with the Travel & Tourism GDP projected to grow at an average 
of 7.1% per annum. The sector contributed approximately  
$ 199.6 Bn to India’s GDP in CY 2022 and is expected to reach 
$ 512 Bn by CY 2028. The growth of the sector is driven by 
various factors, including India’s geographical diversity, its rich 
cultural heritage, and diverse natural beauty. The increasing 
middle-income group, higher disposable incomes, and the 
growing domestic tourism market have been key drivers of this 
growth.
In spite of the challenges faced, the outlook for the industry 
continues to be optimistic, with an anticipated rise in demand 
to support ongoing growth. The government’s efforts towards 
the enhancement of tourist destinations, infrastructure 
facilities, and the promotion of various segments of tourism, 
further bolster the industry’s growth and establish India as a 
progressively favored destination for international travelers.Go
vernment Initiatives
Government initiatives have played a crucial role in boosting 
the Travel & Tourism sector. The expansion of e-Visa facilities, 
the promotion of pilgrimage tourism through the PRASHAD 
Scheme, and the development of tourist circuits under Swadesh 
Darshan Scheme are just a few examples. These initiatives, 
alongside significant investments in infrastructure, are driving 
the growth of the tourism industry, contributing to job creation 
and foreign exchange earnings. The government has adopted 
a mission-oriented strategy to propel tourism during the Amrit 
Kaal, accompanied by a strategic roadmap for the next 25 
years. The ambition is to transform India into a premier global 
travel destination by 2047, creating an unmatched allure for 
visitors from around the world.
P
erformance overview
Thomas Cook India Group recorded a profit in FY25 with a 
healthy contribution from every business and geography to the 
profitability. Total Income for FY25 was at ` 82,845.3 Mn as 
compared to ` 74,356.5 Mn in FY24 reporting a growth of 11%. 
Consolidated EBITDA for the FY25 increased to ` 6216.6 Mn 
from ` 5,717.7 Mn for FY24. This success can be attributed 
to the customer centricity, volume growth, increased digital 
initiatives and Company’s strategic focus on cost optimization. 
The Company’s prudent financial management is evident from 
its robust position, with substantial cash and bank balances 
held as of March 31, 2025 which stood at ` 20.7 Bn.

PROMO
TERS
Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited
The Promoter of your Company, Fairbridge Capital (Mauritius) 
Limited (“FCML ”) is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Fairfax 
Financial Holdings Limited (“Fairfax”), a company incorporated 
under the laws of Canada and listed on the Toronto Stock 
Exchange.
Fairfax is a holding company which, through its subsidiaries, 
is primarily engaged in property and casualty insurance and 
reinsurance and the associated investment management. 
Fairfax was founded in 1985 by the present Chair and Chief 
Executive Officer, Mr. Prem Watsa. Fairfax has been under 
present management since 1985 and is headquartered in 
Toronto, Canada. Fairfax’s corporate objective is to achieve 
a high rate of return on invested capital and build long-term 
shareholder value. Since 1985, Fairfax has demonstrated a 
strong financial track record to achieve an annual compounded 
appreciation in book value per share of 18.7% (including 
dividends). As at December 31, 2024, Fairfax has consolidated 
assets of USD 96.8 billion.
Thomas Cook (India) Limited is a part of the Fairfax group. As 
of March 31, 2025, the promoter holds 63.83% of the total paid 
up equity share capital of the Company.

future recurrence. All Information Technology applications and

security features and the entire business operations are back

impact on the Company at present, nor is expected to have any 
material financial impact in the future.
We further report that,  as informed by the management, below 
instances of fraud happened during the Audit period:
- Call center staff fraudulently collected customer’s 
booking amount under his own personal bank account 
by deliberately sharing his personal bank details with the 
customer by manually changing the bank account details in his signature. The siphoned amount is INR 3.39 lakhs. 
The Police complaint has been filed.
- The staff who was working as BT/CT executive handling 
visa requests for Thomas Cook (India) Limited & SOTC 
Travel Limited’s corporate customers, has violated the 
process to steal advances given to him for submission of 
visa requests, causing financial loss to the Company. The 
Staff has been terminated. 
- a series of online fraudulent transactions were reported 
against different Axis Bank corporate cards which were 
used internationally bypassing multi factor authentication 
(OTP) process as claimed by cardholders. The dispute has 
been raised with the Bank. 
- Victim claimed that his ICICI Bank Credit Card was 
misused by scammer in the pretext of increasing credit 
card limit. The Victim also claimed that his phone was 
hacked on call and money was fraudulently debited on 
his card on SOTC Travel Limited’s website by taking the 
OTP from his phone. Upon checking the Company’s Bank 
Accounts and Payment gateway, there was no such bank 
credit of the amount and the same was informed to Cyber 
Crime Department.

ANNUAL REPORT ON CORPORATE SOCIAL 
RESPONSIBILITY (CSR) ACTIVITIES FOR FY 2024-25
1. BRIEF OUTLINE ON CSR POLICY OF THE COMPANY:
 CSR vision:
 Thomas Cook (India) Limited exists not only for doing good business, but equally to do good for society.
 As a result of this holistic vision, aimed at achieving long-term stakeholder value creation, the Company seamlessly integrates 
its CSR efforts with its pursuit of business excellence in a mutually beneficial manner.
 Thomas Cook (India) Limited shall always continue to respect the interests of and be responsive towards the communities it 
serves and operates in - especially those from socially and economically backward groups, the underprivileged and marginalized; 
thereby, society at large.
 “As an integral part of our commitment to Good Corporate Citizenship, we at Thomas Cook (India) Limited will actively work to 
improve the quality of life of the people in the communities we serve. We shall relentlessly strive to partner with  the Government, 
respected socially conscious agencies and NGOs in the noble efforts of nation-building via sustainable economic & social 
development, inclusive growth and social equity”.
 CSR Char
ter & Focus:
 In our CSR journey, we shall selectively deploy our financial resources earmarked for CSR to drive an action agenda in line 
with Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013 as recommended by the CSR Committee of the Company and overseen by the 
Management and nominated representatives from the Board of Directors.
 The Company’s annual CSR budget and efforts shall focus on:
1. Health and Sanitation:
 Improving access to healthcare by focusing on developing a high impact, holistic, sustainable and collaborative ecosystem 
that offers free/ affordable, quality healthcare services to underprivileged population in parts of India where there is limited 
healthcare infrastructure/ access including undertaking Project Dialysis through Fairfax India Charitable Foundation by 
collaborating with government on a public private partnership supporting Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Program 
(PMNDP) or supporting private charitable organization thereby developing access to dialysis at parts of India where there 
is poor dialysis infrastructure.
 The locations where the Company has setup Dialysis  Centre are mentioned in Annexure A herein below.
 Addressing lack of hygiene and sanitation facilities at tourist spots Pan India or on highways enroute to these tourist spots. 
This will be done by setting up/managing environment friendly toilet facilities and the underprivileged local population will 
be trained in the upkeep of these facilities.
2. Any other Project or Programme that falls under the purview of Schedule VII of Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, 
as identified and approved from time to time.

c. A brief on types of customers
 Thomas Cook (India) Limited serves a diverse range of customers seeking travel and tourism services. We cater to individual 
travellers, families, corporate clients, leisure travellers, honeymooners, adventure seekers, senior citizens, students, special 
interest groups and non-resident Indians (NRIs). With a commitment to providing comprehensive travel solutions, the company 
ensures that each customer’s unique needs are met. Our customers are from various parts of the country and of different 
nationalities ranging from individuals to corporate and Government/ Quasi Government bodies/ authorities.

TION B: MANAGEMENT AND PROCESS DISCLOSURES
This section describes the structures, policies and processes aligned to nine principles of business responsibility. These 
briefly are as follows: 
P1:  Businesses should conduct and govern themselves with Ethics, Transparency and Accountability 
P2:  Businesses should provide goods and services in a manner that is sustainable and safe 
P3:  Businesses should respect and promote the well-being of all employees, including those in their value chains 
P4:  Businesses should respect the interests of and be responsive to all its stakeholders
P5:  Businesses should respect and promote human rights 
P6:  Businesses should respect and make efforts to protect and restore the environment 
P7:  Businesses, when engaged in influencing public and regulatory policy, should do so in a manner that is responsible and 
transparent 
P8:  Businesses should promote inclusive growth and equitable development 
P9:  Businesses should engage with and provide value to their consumers in a responsible manner

2. Does the entity have processes in place to avoid / manage conflict of interests involving members of the Board? (Yes / No) 
If yes, provide details of the same
 Yes. The Company undertakes assessment in order to identify any and all potential areas for conflict of interest. It engages with 
internal and external stakeholders to ensure the comprehensiveness of this assessment process. Based on the outcomes of 
this assessment process, the Company:
•  Enhances its business practices to eliminate any perceived threat of a conflict of interest occurring;
•		 Reviews	and	re-confirms	the	effectiveness	of	both	its	external	grievance	system	and	associated	internal	systems	through	
which any potential and actual conflicts of interest can be highlighted, investigated and addressed;
•  Provides appropriate training to the Board member/ employee with regard to how to recognise and avoid conflicts of

5. Does the entity have a business continuity and disaster management plan?
 Yes, The Company has a Business Continuity Policy. An effective Business Continuity Management System is absolutely 
necessary to continue our operations and add stakeholder value. As the pandemic has shown, business disruptions can come 
in many forms and such external factors are rarely in our control. Business continuity plans and the governance processes 
around it are therefore given the utmost importance by TCIL to attain its strategic objectives. This is achieved through the 
following:
A. Implementation of an effective enterprise risk management framework including documentation of detailed policies and 
procedures
B.	 An	efficient	process	of	identification,	monitoring	and	mitigation	of	risks	–	both	internal	and	external
C. Working closely with all internal and external stakeholders including employees, customers, supplier partners, etc for 
addressing emerging risks and ensuring the safety of all concerned
D. Allocating adequate resources to business continuity planning and disaster management in the event of unforeseen 
exigencies including executing periodic drills, ensuring access to systems for critical resources, and working with the 
relevant authorities
E. Training of staff for ensuring adherence to internal business continuity plans and appropriate regulatory requirements

OBAL ECONOMIC OVERVIEW 
The global economy in CY 2025 is forecast to grow at a reduced 
rate of 2.8%, a signiﬁcant drop from the growth rate of 3.7% (CY 
2000–CY 2019). This slowdown is largely inﬂuenced by rising 
trade tensions, particularly the introduction of substantial tariﬀs 
by key economies, which have disrupted global trade networks. 
The growth trajectory of advanced economies reﬂects this 
volatility, with the United States expected to slow to 1.8% in 
CY 2025, primarily due to softer demand and persistent trade 
conﬂicts. The Euro Area will also face slower growth, projected at 
just 0.8%, as the region grapples with the eﬀects of the tariﬀs and 
other uncertainties. However, there is a silver lining with Spain, 
showing stronger performance with a 2.5% growth rate, driven 
by the carryover from CY 2024 and reconstruction activities.
Emerging markets and developing economies (EMDEs) are 
similarly impacted, with China’s growth forecast lowered to 
4.0% due to the ongoing trade disruptions, although it beneﬁts 
from stronger carryovers from 2024. On the other hand, 
India maintains a relatively stable growth forecast of 6.5%, 
underpinned by robust domestic consumption, despite the 
global uncertainty.
Global trade volume growth is anticipated to remain sluggish 
at 1.7%, reﬂecting the cascading eﬀects of these trade tensions. 
Additionally, inﬂation is expected to rise globally, with headline 
inﬂation projected at 4.3%, driven by higher costs from supply 
chain disruptions and trade measures.
Geopolitical Risks 
During the year, the global geopolitical landscape remained 
dynamic, with regional conﬂicts, policy shifts, and strategic 
tensions inﬂuencing economic sentiment and operational risks 
across sectors.
•  The Russia–Ukraine conﬂict continued through this period 
with no material resolution. The sustained disruption 
to energy and commodity ﬂows, particularly in Eastern 
Europe, inﬂuenced pricing volatility and contributed to 
cautious investment sentiment in aﬀected regions.
•  In the Middle East, tensions persisted, with intermittent 
escalations in late 2024 and early 2025.
A signiﬁcant policy shift occurred as the United States 
implemented a broad set of tariﬀs on a range of imported 
goods, citing economic and strategic considerations. These 
measures led to a brief correction in global equity markets and 
added to global trade uncertainty.
(Source: IMF Report)INDIA ECONOMIC O
VERVIEW
India’s economy is poised for signiﬁcant advancement, with a 
projected nominal GDP of USD 4.19 tn in CY 2025, making it 
the fourth-largest economy globally, just ahead of Japan. This 
marks a notable milestone in India’s economic journey, having 
been the ﬁfth-largest economy in CY 2024. The country’s steady 
rise reﬂects improving domestic economic fundamentals, such 
as strong rural consumption, an expanding infrastructure 
base, and consistent policy support aimed at fostering growth. 
Sectors like automotive, FMCG, electronics, pharmaceuticals, 
and renewable energy continue to lead in driving economic 
expansion. The automotive industry has seen robust growth, 
while India is establishing itself as a manufacturing hub for 
electronics. Additionally, the pharmaceuticals sector remains 
a vital contributor to global supply chains. The government’s 
focus on digital transformation, infrastructure development, and 
green technologies, including electric vehicles and renewable 
energy, is expected to provide further growth opportunities. 
Furthermore, India’s ﬁntech ecosystem has emerged as the 
third-highest funded globally in CY 2025, showcasing the 
country’s digital innovation in ﬁnancial services. Despite 
challenges such as agricultural production ﬂuctuations and 
global trade uncertainties, India’s growing middle class, strong 
labour force, and consumer base support its optimistic growth 
trajectory. By CY 2027, India is projected to surpass the USD 5 
tn mark and is on track to become the third-largest economy 
by CY 2028, overtaking Germany.
Outlook
India
’s economic outlook remains strong, driven by structural 
reforms, policy support, and technological advancements. 
Despite global trade uncertainties and geopolitical risks, the 
country’s growth rate remains among the highest for major 
economies. Robust domestic demand, steady government 
expenditure, and productivity gains will sustain economic 
resilience. Investments in infrastructure, digital transformation, 
and sustainable technologies will fuel long-term growth. India 
is set to surpass the USD 5 tn mark by CY 2027 and become 
the third-largest economy by CY 2028, further cementing its 
role in the global economic landscape.

Travel and Tourism Industry

supply chains supporting agricultural producers, food service providers, retail establishments, ﬁnancial institutions and countless 
small businesses. Indeed, more than two-thirds of the sector’s economic contribution ﬂows through indirect or induced channels, 
including supply chain eﬀects, government spending and capital investment.

Global Hospitality Industry 
The global hospitality industry, covering lodging, food and 
beverage, and tourism services, was valued at USD 5,384.78 
bn in CY 2024 and is expected to grow to USD 5,717.43 bn in 
CY 2025, with a CAGR of 6.2%. By CY 2029, it is projected to 
reach USD 7,239.02 bn, maintaining a CAGR of 6.1% between 
CY 2025-CY 2029. Growth is driven by economic expansion, 
the recovery of tourism, and technological advancements. As 
international tourism rises, the demand for hospitality services 
increases, with innovations like AI, automation, contactless 
systems, and mobile payments improving guest experiences 
and eﬃciency. Trends like personalisation, sustainability, and 
wellness tourism are becoming more prominent, as consumers 
seek tailored, eco-friendly, and health-conscious experiences. 
Asia-Paciﬁc leads the market, with countries like China, India, 
Japan, and Indonesia investing heavily in infrastructure. North 
America and the Middle East, particularly the UAE and Saudi 
Arabia, are also experiencing strong growth due to signiﬁcant 
investments in hospitality infrastructure. These factors position 
the industry for continued growth and innovation.Global Hospitality Industry Growth Overview

Global Imaging Industry
The resurgence of global travel, driven by better connectivity 
and rising incomes, 
has made tourism an experience-focussed 
pursuit. As travellers seek cultural richness and personalised 
adventures, capturing these moments has become essential, 
positioning the photography industry as a key player in the 
travel and tourism ecosystem.
Photography is now deeply embedded in how travellers 
engage with destinations, as they increasingly want to 
document and share unique experiences. This has led to 
greater demand for high-quality visual content, especially in 
scenic, historic, and culturally rich areas. As tourism expands 
into lesser-known regions, the photography industry plays a 
crucial role in destination marketing and personal storytelling.
Digital photography technologies like instant photo printing, 
AI-enhanced images, and online sharing tools meet tourists’ 
demands for convenience and quality, enhancing their overall 
experience. This seamless integration of exploration and 
memory-making fosters repeat visits and positive word-of-
mouth.

Outlook
The global T
ravel & Tourism industry is set for strong growth in 
CY 2025, with international visitor spending reaching USD 2.1 
tn, up from USD 1.9 tn in CY 2019. The sector’s contribution to 
the global economy is projected at USD 11.7 tn (10.3% of global 
GDP), supporting 14 mn new jobs. While Europe recovers 
strongly, the U.S. faces challenges, and China’s growth is 
expected to slow. Saudi Arabia plans to invest USD 800 bn 
in tourism by CY 2030. By CY 2035, the sector is projected to 
contribute USD 16.5 TN (11.5% of global GDP). 
Global Foreign Ex
change Industry
The global foreign exchange (forex) market was valued at  
USD 861 bn in CY 2024 and is projected to reach USD 1,535 bn 
by CY 2033, growing at a CAGR of 6.64%. Key drivers include 
interest rate diﬀerentials, economic indicators like GDP and 
inﬂation, and the growing interconnectedness of ﬁnancial 
markets through digitalisation. The market’s liquidity oﬀers 
signiﬁcant trading opportunities, inﬂuenced by central bank 
policies and geopolitical events.
The Currency Swap segment led the market in CY 2024 with 
a 40.2% share, vital for managing currency risks. Reporting 
Dealers (e.g., banks and ﬁnancial institutions) dominate the 
market as intermediaries.
Regionally, North America holds 25.8% of the market, with the 
U.S. responsible for 88.9% of global forex transactions, driven 
by the USD as the primary reserve currency. The Euro plays 
a signiﬁcant role in Europe, while Asia-Paciﬁc sees growth 
from China and Japan. Latin America and the Middle East are 
inﬂuenced by trade and remittance ﬂows.
Indian F
oreign Exchange Industry
The Indian Foreign Exchange (FX) Industry has grown 
signiﬁcantly over the years and plays a crucial role in the 
country’s economy by facilitating currency exchange globally. 
As of 2024, the Indian foreign exchange market size was 
valued at approximately USD 30.7 bn and is projected to grow 
to USD 65.8 bn by 2033, with a compound annual growth 
rate (CAGR) of 8.8% from 2025 to 2033. This growth is driven 
by increased remittances from Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), 
robust foreign exchange reserves, rising Foreign Portfolio 
Investment (FPI) inﬂows, and a strong export sector, especially 
in IT and business services.
In FY 2024–25, outward remittances under the Reserve Bank 
of India’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) stood at USD 
29.56 bn, reﬂecting a 6.85% decline from the previous year. 
Travel continued to dominate outﬂows, accounting for nearly 60% at USD 16.96 bn, with modest year-on-year moderation. 
Education-related remittances fell 16% to USD 2.92 bn, and 
medical expenses abroad dropped over 55%. Conversely, 
investment segments recorded robust growth, with overseas 
equity and debt investments up 12.5% to USD 1.70 bn and 
purchases of immovable property overseas rising 33% to USD 
320 mn. The year ended with a 10.6% surge in March 2025 
remittances, driven by travel and investment activity.  
Indian T
ravel and Tourism Industry Overview
The Indian travel and tourism industry is a signiﬁcant sector 
within the Indian economy, projected to generate revenue 
exceeding USD 59 bn by CY 2028, which is over /uni20B9 5,12,356 
crores. Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs) are expected to reach 
30.5 mn by CY 2028, a substantial increase from 9.52 mn in 
CY 2023, which saw a 47.9% growth compared to the previous 
year. The travel market in India is expected to reach USD 125 
bn by FY 2026-27, up from an estimated USD 75 bn in FY 
2019-20.
According to World Travel & Tourism Council, the industry 
is expected to grow at an annual rate of 7.1% in the coming 
decade, with the Travel & Tourism GDP projected to grow 
at an average of 7.1% per annum. The sector contributed 
approximately USD 199.6 bn to India’s GDP in CY 2022 and 
is expected to reach USD 512 bn by CY 2028. The growth 
of the sector is driven by various factors, including India’s 
geographical diversity, its rich cultural heritage, and diverse 
natural beauty. The increasing middle-income group, higher 
disposable incomes, and the growing domestic tourism market 
have been key drivers of this growth. Government initiatives 
have played a crucial role in boosting the Travel & Tourism 
sector. The expansion of e-Visa facilities, the promotion of 
pilgrimage tourism through the PRASHAD Scheme, and the 
development of tourist circuits under Swadesh Darshan 
Scheme are just a few examples. These initiatives, alongside 
signiﬁcant investments in infrastructure, are driving the growth 
of the tourism industry, contributing to job creation and foreign 
exchange earnings. The government has adopted a mission-
oriented strategy to propel tourism during the Amrit Kaal, 
accompanied by a strategic roadmap for the next 25 years. 
The ambition is to transform India into a premier global travel 
destination by 2047, creating an unmatched allure for visitors 
from around the world.
Spiritual Tourism/Pilgrimage Travel: The segment is expanding 
due to the development of key pilgrimage sites like Ayodhya, 
with the construction of hotels and infrastructure expected to 
meet the growing demand. The IRCTC’s Bharat Darshan tourist 
trains and the government’s focus on pilgrimage rejuvenation 
through the PRASHAD Scheme have further boosted this 
sector.
Medical Tourism: With the government’s ‘Heal in India’ 
initiative, the medical tourism segment is poised to grow at a 0 Thomas Cook

Indian Hospitality Industry Overview
The Indian hospitality mark
et exhibited strong growth in 
CY 2024, with a notable increase in both market size and 
performance. By the end of January 2025, the market 
capitalisation reached /uni20B9 2.5 tn, reﬂecting a healthy ﬁnancial 
outlook for the sector. Debt levels among major hotel ownership 
groups have reduced signiﬁcantly, reducing ﬁnancial risks and 
opening the door for more investment and acquisitions.
The industry showed impressive performance metrics, 
including a 10.7% increase in revenue per available room in  
CY 2024 compared to CY 2023, and room revenue per day 
that was 82% higher than in CY 2019, marking a complete 
recovery from the pandemic years. Demand absorption was 
robust, with 123k rooms demanded per day, a 30% increase 
over CY 2019. Additionally, supply grew by 32%, supporting 
the industry’s expansion while maintaining demand across 
both traditional and emerging markets.

Outlook
India
’s tourism sector is on a strong growth path, with its GDP 
contribution projected to rise from USD 178 bn in CY 2019 to 
USD 512 bn by CY 2028. The travel market is expected to grow 
from USD 75 bn in FY 2019-20 to USD 125 bn by FY 2026-
27, driven by rising demand, improved infrastructure, and

support job creation and drive long-term economic growth.
Business Overview
Thomas 
Cook (India) Limited(referred to as ‘TCIL’ or ‘the 
Company’), established in 1881, is a leading integrated travel 
and ﬁnancial services company headquartered in India. Backed 
by the Fairfax Group, which holds a 63.83% equity stake, TCIL 
operates across 28 countries and ﬁve continents through a 
diversiﬁed and customer-centric business model.
The Company oﬀers a comprehensive portfolio across four 
core verticals: travel and travel related services, foreign 
exchange, hospitality, and digital imaging. Its travel segment 
comprising leisure holidays, destination management, 
corporate travel, and MICE was the largest contributor 
in FY 2024-25, accounting for approximately 79% of the 
consolidated revenue. TCIL is also India’s largest non-bank 
forex service provider, supported by an extensive physical 
and digital network. Under the Sterling brand, the Company 
manages a nationwide resort chain focussed on experiential 
hospitality, while its digital imaging business under DEI 
delivers tech-enabled photography solutions at major global 
attractions. Together, these businesses form an integrated 
platform delivering end-to-end travel and ﬁnancial solutions.

Digital Imaging Solutions, operated by Digiphoto Entertainment 
Imaging 
Limited (DEI), provides imaging services, experiential 
products, and innovative technology at global attractions. 
DEI works with 129 partners across theme parks, tall towers, 
aquariums, water parks, luxury hotels, cable cars, snow parks, 
and animal/bird parks. Headquartered in Dubai, it operates in 
18 countries across 3 continents, managing 271 sites through 
129 partnerships and employing 2,400+ professionals. In  
FY 2024-25, DEI captured over 130 mn images.
In FY 2024-25, performance was impacted by adverse 
weather, geopolitical tensions, and seasonal shifts, resulting 
in a 9% drop in income to /uni20B9 8,423 mn and a 51% decline in 
EBIT to /uni20B9 268 mn. The Company exited certain markets, while 
strengthening its presence in proﬁtable regions. Despite the 
challenges, DEI achieved a 100% renewal rate for 50+ accounts 
and secured 30 new partnerships.
To enhance eﬃciency and guest experience, DEI is 
implementing its new WeC platform, featuring AI-enabled 
tools such as face recognition, auto-editing, and instant image 
delivery.

Credit Ratings Upgraded by CRISIL
In June 2025, CRISIL has upgraded the long-term rating and 
corporate credit rating (CCR) of Thomas Cook (India) Limited 
(TCIL) to ‘CRISIL AA/Stable’ from ‘CRISIL AA-/Positive’. The 
short-term rating has been reaﬃrmed at ‘CRISIL A1+.
CRISIL Ratings has combined the business and ﬁnancial 
risk proﬁles of TCIL and its subsidiaries, including Sterling 
Holiday Resorts Ltd (Sterling), TC Tours Ltd (CRISIL AA-/Stable/
CRISIL A1+), Travel Corporation India Ltd (CRISIL AA/Stable), 
SOTC Travel Ltd (CRISIL AA/Stable/CRISIL A1+), Travel Circle 
International Ltd, Horizon Travel Services LLC, Travel Circle 
International (Mauritius) Ltd, and Digiphoto Entertainment 
Imaging Limited (DEI). This is because all these entities, 
collectively referred to as the Thomas Cook India Group (or 
‘Group’), are strategically important to, and have considerable 
operational integration with TCIL.
This upgrade in CRISIL’s long-term rating to ‘AA/Stable’ 
represents the highest credit rating in Thomas Cook India’s 
history. Also, this is the highest credit rating for any travel and 
tourism company in India. As leaders in India’s travel & tourism 
industry, it also reﬂects the Company’s growth in earnings, 
strong balance sheet, long-term resilience and sustainability 
measures - coupled with the upgrade in our parent company’s 
credit rating to ‘A-/Stable’. The upgraded rating for TCIL also 
recognises the continued trust and commitment of Fairfax 
Financial Holdings to the Thomas Cook India Group. As we 
look ahead, this recognition enhances our ability to scale with 
conﬁdence and deliver greater value to our customers and 
stakeholders.
Yield (on Investments) Optimisation in a Falling Interest Rate 
Regime
Following the ‘Safety First’ principle, as always, the Company 
prioritised investments in bank deposits and selectively invested in a limited number of mutual funds, all of which were 
in line with the pre-approved board policy. In response to the 
global decline in interest rates for multiple currencies, we 
adopted strategies to enhance yield. This involved extensive 
usage of currency swaps to move funds across currencies and 
countries on a fully hedged basis. 
Support to Subsidiaries
As business activity normalised across most geographies 
during FY 2024-25, the need for inter-company ﬁnancial 
assistance to Indian and overseas subsidiaries signiﬁcantly 
declined, with support extended sparingly. Selective aid was 
provided to subsidiaries in slower-recovering markets to 
enable critical payments and sustain operational continuity. The 
Company encouraged subsidiaries to become independent by 
increasing bank lines wherever needed by working closely with 
the central treasury team. The subsidiaries made repayments 
of around ` 1 bn during the ﬁnancial year.

Project Dialysis
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) aﬀects nearly one in seven 
adults in India, with over 1.3 mn individuals requiring dialysis 
two 
to three times a week to survive. However, due to the 
high cost of treatment and limited accessibility, only about 
15% of patients currently receive the care they need. While the 
country requires more than 200,000 dialysis machines, only 
around 35,000 are operational—predominantly serving urban 
and aﬄuent populations.
In response to this urgent healthcare gap, Thomas Cook India 
has forged strategic alliances with state governments and 
hospitals across the country. The Company is committed to 
creating an ecosystem that enables free or aﬀordable, high-
quality dialysis services for patients, particularly in underserved 
and rural areas. Through this initiative, the Company aspires 
to alleviate the burden of CKD and meaningfully improve 
patient outcomes and quality of life. For further details on the 
initiatives, please refer to the Integrated Report on page 71.0 Thomas Cook ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------· -------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

162Internal Control S
ystems and Their Adequacy
At Thomas Cook India, robust internal control systems are 
embedded across all functions and processes. These systems 
are continuously reviewed and reﬁned to enhance operational 
eﬃciency, eﬀectiveness, and governance. An annual Internal 
Audit plan, approved by the Audit Committee, ensures 
systematic evaluation of processes. This is complemented by 
IT Auditors, Internal Financial Auditors and Statutory Auditors, 
who validate the accuracy of ﬁnancial reporting and the 
eﬀectiveness of control mechanisms.
In compliance with RBI guidelines, the Company has instituted 
Concurrent Auditing for its Foreign Exchange operations 
across branches. The Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Policy is 
regularly updated to reﬂect regulatory changes, and measures 
are in place to ensure adherence to audit trail requirements.
Audit ﬁndings are thoroughly discussed with Senior 
Management and reviewed quarterly by the Audit Committee, 
reinforcing a culture of accountability and continuous

t of the Directors on Corporate Governance
1. COMPANY’S PHILOSOPHY ON THE CODE OF CORPORATE GOVERNANCE:
 Thomas Cook (India) Limited (“TCIL/Company”) philosophy on Corporate Governance is to conduct its business in a manner 
which is ethical and transparent with all stakeholders of the Company. The Company believes in providing a structure that works 
for the benefit of everyone concerned, by ensuring that the Company adheres to ethical standards, laws and best practices. The 
Company’s policy on Corporate Governance is to make it a way of life by, inter-alia , adopting standard Corporate Governance 
practices through continual improvement of internal systems and satisfaction of customers and shareholders. The Company 
in its approach to adopt the best possible practices of Corporate Governance and keeping adherence to the latest rules and 
regulations prescribed by various regulatory authorities, has taken all the necessary steps to stay in line with the continuously 
progressing governance demands.
 TCIL endeavours to demonstrate the highest standards of Corporate Governance and ethical behaviour across all levels within 
the organisation with a zero-tolerance policy towards any deviation from these standards. Our ethical framework focuses on 
long term shareholder value creation through responsible decision making. As a global organisation, the Corporate Governance 
practices followed by the Company and its subsidiaries are compatible with international standards and practices.
 Our Corporate Governance framework ensures that we make timely disclosures and share relevant information regarding our 
financial performance, as well as disclosure related to the leadership and governance of the Company. At TCIL, Corporate 
Governance is more than just adherence to the statutory and regulatory requirements. It is equally about focusing on voluntary 
practices that underline the highest levels of transparency and propriety.
 Over the years, the Board of Directors has developed Corporate Governance guidelines to help fulfill our corporate responsibility 
towards the Company’s stakeholders. These guidelines ensure that the Board will have the necessary authority and processes 
to review and evaluate the Company’s operations when required. Further, these guidelines allow the Board to make decisions 
that are independent of the Management. The Board may change these guidelines as and when required, to achieve the 
Company’s stated objectives.
2. 
BOARD OF DIRECTORS (“BOARD”):
 TCIL, as a Company believes that an active, well informed and independent Board is necessary to ensure the highest standards 
of Corporate Governance. The Company believes that the Board is at the core of Corporate Governance and thus has optimum 
mix of Executive and Non Executive Directors; including Woman Director, which plays a significant role in ensuring the highest 
standards of Corporate Governance practice in the Company.
 Size and Composition of the Board:
 The Composition of the TCIL Board as on March 31, 2025, included eleven (11) members with two (2) Executive Directors and 
nine (9) Non Executive Directors, of which six (6) were Independent Directors including one (1) Woman Independent Director, 
comprising of experts from various fields/professions.
 The composition of the Board of Directors of the Company is in accordance with the Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and the Companies Act, 2013, read with applicable rules 
made thereunder, as amended from time to time.
 Key Skills, Expertise and Competencies of the Board:
 The Board of Directors of TCIL comprises of qualified members who have the skills, expertise and competence to make effective 
contribution to the growth of the Company as well as on the various business and governance matters discussed in the Board 
and Committee meetings. The Board Members are committed to ensure that the Company is in compliance with the requisite 
standards of Corporate Governance.0 Thomas Cook ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------· -------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

only ensures high standards of security and confidentiality, required for storage and circulation of Board papers but also increases

and Regulation 16(1)(b) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, as amended. Based on the disclosures received from the Independent Directors, the Board has confirmed 
that they meet the criteria of Independence as mentioned under Section 149(6) of the Companies Act, 2013, read with Regulation 
16(1)(b) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, 
as amended from time to time. The Board of Directors, based on the declaration(s) received from the Independent Directors, 
have verified the veracity of such disclosures and confirm that the Independent Directors fulfill the conditions of independence 
specified in the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 
and the Companies Act, 2013, as amended and are independent of the management of the Company. Further all Independent 
Directors have confirmed that there is no change in the circumstances which may affect their status as an Independent Director 
and they are not aware of any circumstances or situation, which exist or may be reasonably anticipated, that could impair or 
impact their ability to discharge their duties with an objective independent judgment and without any external influence.
 In the opinion of the Board, they fulfill the condition for appointment/ re-appointment as Independent Directors on the Board. 
Further, in the opinion of the Board, the Independent Directors also possess the attributes of integrity, expertise and experience 
for appointment/ re-appointment as Independent Directors on the Board of the Company and they are Independent of the 
management.
